title: SmarTrend Weekly Wrap Up: May 14, 2010
text:
SmarTrend Weekly Wrap Up: May 14, 2010 April 15, 2018 by admin Leave a Comment 
•The European Union unveils the euro $966 billion mega-fund aimed at staving off disaster from the debt contagion crisis, includes 440 billion euros in loans from eurozone nations, 60 billion euros from the EU emergency funds and 250 billion from the IMF 
•Peabody Energy (NYSE:BTU) lowered its offer for Macarthur Coal following Australias 40% mining tax proposal. Macarthur later in the week abandons Gloucester Coal merger to consider bid 
•Telefonica (NYSE:TEF) offered $7.3 billion cash for the 50% stake Portugal Telecom owns in Brasilcel NV 
•Boeing (NYSE:BA), BAE Systems and Raytheon (NYSE:RTN) in talks to acquire Argon ST (NASDAQ:STST) 
•Toyota Motor (NYSE:TM) posts better-than-expected fourth quarter profit, but operating profit forecast disappoints 
•Carl Icahn raised his stake in Motorola (NYSE:MOT) to approximately 8.75% 
•Sprint (NYSE:S) scraps plans to make Googles (NASDAQ:GOOG) Nexus One available on its network 
•The Senate votes in overwhelming favor (96-0) of a measure that would require the government to conduct an unprecedented one-time audit of the Federal Reserve 
•Verizon (NYSE:VZ) and Google (NASDAQ:GOOG) team up on iPad (NASDAQ:AAPL) rival 
•SAP AG (NYSE:SAP) acquires Sybase (NYSE:SY) for $65 per share, or approximately $5.8 billion 
•A Canadian court ruled that Lions Gate Entertainments (NYSE:LGF) poison pill plan was illegal, but a majority of shareholders backed the plan 
•The Senate approves (64-35) making a clearinghouse intermediary that chooses credit rating agencies for financial institutions on a semi-random basis
